name: Short Call Condor
summary: Sell the outer calls and buy the two middle calls for a net credit; profits if the underlying moves outside the outer strikes - a long-volatility structure in all calls.
max_profit: net credit x 100, outside strikes A and D
max_loss: (W1 - net credit) x 100, between B and C
when_to_use: IV rank <= 25 with an expected breakout. Payoff-equivalent to a long (reverse) iron condor at the same strikes - route whichever is priced better.
entry_rules: Net credit >= 55% of W1 (equivalently, max loss <= 45% of width)
Body wide enough that the breakout distance is <= 1.0 x expected move
OI >= 500 and spread <= 10% of mid on all four strikes
Alpaca level 3 (defined risk: short A is covered by long B, short D is naked-looking but covered by long C at a lower strike)
Compare against the reverse iron condor at the same strikes and route the better fill
management_rules: Take profit at 60% of max profit
Close within 30 minutes of the open after a scheduled catalyst
Loss stop at 50% of max loss
exit_rules: Force-close by 15:45 ET on expiration day, always
The lowest strike A is a SHORT ITM call from entry - close or roll it before any ex-dividend date whenever its extrinsic < the projected dividend
Close immediately if short A's extrinsic < $0.10 or its delta >= 0.90
Close when spot exceeds D or falls below A by more than 0.5 x W1 (at/near max profit)
assignment_risk: High: short call A is deep ITM from entry. Dividend-driven early assignment is the dominant risk. Prefer the reverse iron condor expression, which puts the short legs OTM.
liquidity_needs: ITM call strikes must be quotable; OI >= 500 per leg.
common_mistakes: Not realizing the deep ITM short call is an assignment magnet; treating the credit as income when it is really the flip side of a debit structure.
zero_dte_notes: Avoid - deep ITM short call on expiration day.
family: four-leg structures (iron condors, iron butterflies, condors, double calendars/diagonals, boxes, jelly rolls, conversions/reversals, double verticals, double ratio spreads)
